title: Sending notification SMS through a provider API
name: SMS provider client

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles the provider credentials? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The error log for non-2xx responses includes request.headers, which contains the Authorization header with the base64-encoded accountSid:authToken. Base64 is trivially reversible, so every 4xx/5xx (including routine 400s for bad numbers) writes the provider auth token into the log pipeline, where anyone with log access can use it to send SMS as the company. Logging only url and status (or a redacted header set) fixes it.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The provider takes longer than SMS_TIMEOUT_MS to respond. What does send do?
choices: Waits indefinitely, because fetch has no default timeout
Logs 'sms provider rejected message' with status 0 and throws a non-retryable error
Logs 'sms transport failure' with cause TimeoutError and throws a retryable SmsSendError
choiceQuestions.explanation: AbortSignal.timeout aborts the fetch, which rejects; the catch logs the error name (TimeoutError) and throws SmsSendError with retryable=true. There is no Response, so the !res.ok branch is not reached and no sid is returned.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A worker retries send after a transport failure, but the provider had actually accepted the first request. What prevents a duplicate SMS, assuming the provider honours the header?
choices: The Idempotency-Key header set to notificationId
The Basic auth header, which binds requests to the account
maskPhone, which makes repeated numbers indistinguishable
choiceQuestions.explanation: Each request carries Idempotency-Key: msg.notificationId, which stays the same across retries of the same notification, letting the provider deduplicate. Authorization identifies the account, not the message; maskPhone affects only logs.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Which provider responses cause send to throw an error marked retryable?
choices: Status 429 and any status 500 or above
choiceQuestions.explanation: The retryable flag is res.status >= 500 || res.status === 429. Other 4xx such as 400 or 401 are not retryable, so 'any non-2xx' and 'only 4xx' are wrong, and 'only 503' is too narrow.
